transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. Before we get into details, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I came in because my mind keeps going blank at the worst times. I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms or holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years.
During these episodes, do you ever lose awareness of what's happening around you, or has anyone told you that you stare blankly or make unusual movements while it's happening?
I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed losing awareness, and nobody’s told me I stare or do anything unusual. It just feels like I can’t pull up what I need in the moment.
During these episodes when your mind goes blank, do you also notice physical symptoms like your heart racing, sweating, trembling, or trouble breathing?
I haven’t really noticed anything physical like that. It’s more just my mind goes blank.

Do these episodes of your mind going blank tend to happen specifically when you feel you're being watched or judged by others, or do they occur unpredictably even when you're alone or not under that kind of pressure?

It happens more when I feel like I’m being watched. I’m convinced the city trucks and police radios are keeping tabs on me. If a road sign flashes, or somebody at church lowers their voice, I know it’s a message about me. My sister says it isn’t, but... I don’t think she understands.
How long have you been having these beliefs that the trucks, radios, and people are sending you messages or watching you—days, weeks, or months?
About a year and four months, I think. That’s when the voices and the messages from the signs, trucks, and radios really started.
You mentioned hearing voices—can you tell me more about that, like how often you hear them and what they say?

I hear them when the house is quiet, and sometimes when I’m standing near a work zone. They’re clear as day—calling my name and saying I caused trouble on the block. Nobody else seems to hear them, though.

During this past year and four months, have there been any periods of weeks or more when you felt very depressed, hopeless, or had little energy, or times when you felt unusually elated, full of energy, or needed very little sleep?
Most mornings, I wake up with this heavy, hollow sadness in my chest. It feels like the day is already ruined before I even get out of bed.
Over this past year and four months since the voices and messages started, would you say you've felt this heavy, hollow sadness most of the time, or only during shorter stretches here and there?
Looking back, it’s been most of the time. Even when the voices or the suspicious thoughts weren’t as bad, that heavy depressed feeling was still there.
Has there been a time, lasting two weeks or more, when you were hearing the voices or having these suspicious beliefs but did NOT have that heavy, depressed feeling?

Yes. Before the depression got so deep, there were several weeks where I was still going to work and church, but I was already hearing my name and thinking the signs and radios were sending messages about me.
Do you use alcohol, cannabis, or any other recreational drugs, and have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions like thyroid problems or neurological issues?
I’m not really sure what would count. I haven’t been told I have any medical problems like that.
Thinking back over the full year and four months, roughly how many weeks or months was it before the depression set in, compared to how long you've been depressed since then?

It was several weeks, I think, where I was still going to work and church, but I was already hearing my name and thinking the signs and radios were about me. Then the depression got much deeper after that.
Since that first stretch of several weeks, has the depressed feeling been present continuously most days up until now, or has it come and gone with breaks where you felt back to your normal mood?

Looking back, it’s been there most days since then. Even when the voices or those suspicious thoughts weren’t as bad, I still felt that heavy depression. I don’t think I really had a break where I felt like my normal self again.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome in. Before we get into details, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports auditory hallucinations (voices calling name, accusing) and persecutory delusions (belief that trucks, radios, signs are surveilling/messaging him) persisting for ~16 months. Critically, there was a distinct period of several weeks where psychotic symptoms occurred without any mood disturbance, satisfying the requirement for psychotic symptoms in the absence of mood episode. Subsequently, a major depressive syndrome (pervasive low mood, hopelessness, anhedonia, low energy) developed and has persisted for the majority of the illness duration, overlapping with ongoing psychotic symptoms. No manic/hypomanic symptoms were reported. No substance use or medical condition was identified as a cause. This pattern—concurrent mood and psychotic symptoms with a required period of psychosis alone, and mood symptoms present for a substantial portion of the total illness duration—is diagnostic of Schizoaffective Disorder, depressive type (F25.1), rather than pure Schizophrenia (which would require mood symptoms to be brief/absent) or Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features (which would require psychosis only during mood episodes).

No blank staring, loss of awareness, or unusual movements reported (argues against seizure/dissociative episodes)
Persistent heavy, hollow sadness most mornings

Denies palpitations, sweating, trembling, or breathing difficulty during blank spells
